engine.hint: Multi-threaded scan, junctions and symlinks skipped
scan.title: Scanning {target}
stat.skipped: {n} folders could not be read (no permission)
confirm.title: Free up
confirm.permWarn: These items will be erased immediately.
confirm.permText: They skip the Recycle Bin and cannot be restored.
confirm.binText: These items will be moved to the Recycle Bin, so you can restore them from there.
confirm.ack: I understand this cannot be undone
empty.title: See what's eating your disk
empty.text: Pick a drive to scan. Tessera walks every folder in parallel and shows you exactly where the space went.
empty.hint: Tip: press F5 any time to rescan.
explorer.hint: Click to zoom · right-click for actions · Backspace to go up
files.name: Name
cleanup.sub: Regenerable caches and build folders. Everything goes to the Recycle Bin.
cleanup.permOn: Permanent delete is on — nothing goes to the Recycle Bin
cleanup.shiftHint: Hold Shift to skip the Recycle Bin
common.scanFirst: Scan a drive or folder first.
settings.languageHint: Detected from your system; English is the fallback
settings.themeHint: Light, dark or follow the system
settings.permHint: Files are erased immediately and space is freed at once.
settings.permBanner: Permanent delete is on. Every delete button now erases files right away — nothing goes to the Recycle Bin.
settings.permConfirmText: From now on every delete in Tessera skips the Recycle Bin and cannot be undone.
settings.shiftHint: One-off permanent delete, even when the setting above is off
settings.protectHint: Windows, Program Files and the page file can't be deleted
settings.autoUpdateHint: Checks GitHub Releases on launch; installs after you confirm the restart
engine.mftHint: Fast path — whole drives in seconds
engine.elevate: Restart as admin for fast scan
scan.subMft: Reading the NTFS Master File Table…
palette.placeholder: Type a command or file name…
update.ready: Update {version} is ready — restart to install
dupes.title: Find identical files
dupes.explain: Files are compared by size, then by a quick hash of their start and end, and finally confirmed with a full BLAKE3 hash. Files under 1 MB are skipped.
dupes.grouping: Grouping by size and quick hash…
history.usageSub: One snapshot per scan · {n} so far
history.needTwo: Scan again later to see how usage changes over time.
history.pick: Pick one to compare with the latest scan
history.noChanges: No folder changed by more than 10 MB.
settings.animationsHint: Motion, transitions and the animated treemap
settings.liveHint: Keeps the results up to date as files change, without a rescan
live.hint: Watching for changes · {n} folders updated since the scan
dupes.linkHint: Keep every path, store the data only once
dupes.linkText: Each extra copy is replaced by a hard link to the kept file. Every path keeps working and {size} is freed.
dupes.linkWarn: Linked copies share their contents: editing one changes all of them. Only works within the same drive.
settings.reopen: Open the last scan on start
settings.reopenHint: No waiting: changes made since then are picked up automatically
cache.savedHint: Opened from your last scan and updated with what changed since. Rescan for a completely fresh one.
cache.caughtUp: Caught up: {n} folders changed since the last scan
cache.caughtUp.one: Caught up: {n} folder changed since the last scan
opt.title: Performance profiles
opt.sub: One click switches the power plan and a set of Windows settings. Your original settings are saved first and can be restored at any time.
opt.profile.gaming.desc: Maximum performance: no background recording, pop-ups or mouse acceleration while you play.
opt.profile.work.desc: Notifications muted so you can concentrate; normal power use.
opt.profile.battery.desc: Longer battery life: power saver plan, fewer effects and background apps.
opt.reboot: Restart Windows to finish applying some of the changes
opt.needAdmin: Some tweaks change machine-wide settings and need administrator rights.
opt.tweaksSub: Fine-tune individual settings; every change can be undone
opt.tweak.game_mode.hint: Windows prioritises the game you're playing
opt.tweak.no_game_dvr.hint: Turns off Xbox Game Bar capture, which costs frames
opt.tweak.perf_visuals.hint: Fewer animations and effects in Windows
opt.tweak.no_transparency.hint: Solid taskbar and menus, less GPU work
opt.tweak.no_background_apps.hint: Store apps can't keep running in the background
opt.tweak.raw_mouse.hint: Turns off "Enhance pointer precision" for consistent aim
opt.tweak.hags.hint: Hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling, lower latency on modern GPUs
opt.tweak.net_throttling.hint: Multimedia scheduler stops throttling the network and reserves less CPU
opt.appsSub: Close what you don't need before a game
opt.appsNone: None of the usual background apps are running
opt.startupSub: Apps that start with Windows; fewer means a faster boot
opt.startupMachine: For all users: needs administrator rights
opt.restoreHint: Every setting, power plan and startup app Tessera changed is put back the way it was.
opt.windowsOnly: The optimizer is available on Windows only.
opt.extrasSub: Situational fixes; profiles never change these
opt.tweak.no_gamebar.hint: Win+G overlay off; Game Mode keeps working
opt.tweak.game_priority.hint: Games get high CPU, GPU and disk priority from the scheduler
opt.tweak.no_power_throttling.hint: Apps always run at full CPU speed, even in the background
opt.tweak.no_web_search.hint: No Bing or web results; search is instant
opt.tweak.no_suggestions.hint: No silently installed apps, tips or Start menu suggestions
opt.tweak.no_mpo.hint: Turns off Multiplane Overlay, the usual cause of stutter with monitors at different refresh rates
opt.tweak.end_task.hint: Right-click a frozen app on the taskbar to close it
opt.tweak.no_activity.hint: Windows stops logging which apps and files you open
opt.tweak.no_update_sharing.hint: Updates come from Microsoft only and are never uploaded to other PCs
junk.temp.hint: Temporary files left behind by apps
junk.pkg_cache.hint: npm, pnpm, pip, NuGet, yarn — re-downloaded on demand
junk.browser.hint: Chrome / Edge / Firefox cache; logins are not touched
engine.adminHint: Fast MFT scans and every system tool are available
engine.userHint: The fast scan and some system tools need administrator rights
rp.creating: Creating a Windows restore point first — this can take a minute
rp.recent: Today's Windows restore point covers this change
rp.skipped: No restore point (System Protection is off); Tessera kept its own backup
rp.skippedAdmin: No restore point without administrator rights; Tessera kept its own backup
rp.willCreate: A Windows restore point is created first, so you can roll back with System Restore.
rp.needsAdmin: Restore points need administrator rights. Tessera still keeps its own backup so you can undo this.
care.headClean: Your PC is in great shape
care.subIntro: Care checks junk files, privacy traces, the registry, shortcuts, startup apps, drive health and software updates in one go.
care.subFree: Fixing frees up {size}. You see everything before anything changes.
care.subNothing: Nothing to clean right now. Check again later or schedule regular scans.
care.fixText: Tessera removes only what the scan found. Details for each part are on its own page.
care.regBackupNote: Registry entries are also backed up by Tessera and can be undone on the Registry page.
care.startupMany: More than usual: boot may be slow
care.settingsSub: What Care checks, what it cleans, and when it runs on its own
care.privacyKindsHint: Cookies and history are off by default: they sign you out of websites and remove your browsing history.
care.autoCleanHint: Scheduled scans also remove safe junk and the privacy items above. The registry is never changed without you.
care.scheduleWindows: Automatic scans use Windows Task Scheduler and are available on Windows.
tray.hidden_body: It keeps working in the tray. Right-click the icon to quit.
tray.care_body: Health score {score}/100 · {size} to clean, {n} issues to fix
settings.closeToTrayHint: The close button hides Tessera; quit from the tray icon
settings.trayMeterHint: The tray icon shows two bars for CPU and memory use
sysjunk.title: System junk
sysjunk.sub: Temporary files, crash dumps and caches in the usual places. No scan needed.
sysjunk.confirmText: These files are deleted directly, not moved to the Recycle Bin. Files that are in use are skipped.
sysjunk.locked: {n} files were in use and were skipped
sysjunk.user_temp.hint: Your temp folder; files from the last 24 hours stay
sysjunk.shaders.hint: DirectX, NVIDIA, AMD; games rebuild them on next start
sysjunk.wu_cache.hint: Downloaded update files older than 3 days
sysjunk.recycle.hint: Empties the Recycle Bin on every drive
sysjunk.logs.hint: App logs older than a day
cleanup.scanForMore: Scan a drive to also find node_modules, build folders and other regenerable caches in your files.
privacy.title: Privacy sweep
privacy.sub: Remove what browsers and Windows remember about what you do. Cookies and history are never picked by default.
privacy.running: Open: only the cache can be cleaned
privacy.closeFirst: Close {names} first to clean cookies and history
privacy.confirmText: The selected traces are deleted. Browsers rebuild their caches when needed.
privacy.confirmRisky: You will be signed out of websites and/or lose your browsing history. Bookmarks and saved passwords are kept.
registry.title: Registry cleaner
registry.sub: Only entries that point to files or folders that no longer exist. Everything removed is backed up and can be undone.
registry.needAdmin: Machine-wide entries can only be fixed as administrator.
registry.confirmText: These entries are removed. Tessera saves a backup first, so you can undo this below.
registry.undoText: {n} entries removed {when} are written back to the registry.
registry.catHint.uninstall: Programs in Installed apps whose files are gone
registry.catHint.app_paths: Program aliases pointing to missing programs
registry.catHint.mui_cache: Names Explorer remembered for deleted programs
shortcuts.title: Broken shortcuts
shortcuts.sub: Shortcuts on the desktop, in the Start menu and on the taskbar whose program is gone.
shortcuts.confirmText: They go to the Recycle Bin.
emptyf.title: Empty folders
emptyf.sub: Folders with nothing inside, from the last scan. System and app data folders are skipped.
emptyf.needScan: Scan a drive to find empty folders.
shred.title: File shredder
shred.sub: Overwrites files before deleting them, so recovery tools can't bring them back.
shred.ssd: On SSDs the drive itself may keep old copies of data blocks out of reach. For SSDs, full-disk encryption is the reliable protection.
shred.confirmText: The files are overwritten and deleted. This can't be undone, not even with recovery tools.
shred.optionHint: Slower, but the files can't be recovered
net.title: Internet booster
net.sub: Pick the fastest DNS for your connection, flush the DNS cache and tune TCP. Every change can be undone.
net.restoreText: DNS servers and TCP settings go back to what they were before Tessera changed them.
net.needAdmin: Changing DNS and TCP settings needs administrator rights.
net.tcpSub: Windows defaults are the right choice for almost everyone; fix them if something turned them off
net.tcp.autotuning.hint: Lets downloads use your full bandwidth
net.tcp.rss.hint: Spreads network work across CPU cores
net.tcp.nagle.hint: Sends small packets right away; can lower ping in online games
net.flushHint: Fixes sites that moved or don't load after a DNS change
net.repairHint: Resets Winsock: the classic fix for "connected but nothing loads"
net.repairText: Winsock is reset and the DNS cache flushed. Restart Windows afterwards.
net.repaired: Network reset; restart Windows to finish
uninst.title: Uninstaller
uninst.sub: Remove programs with their own uninstaller, then clean up the folders and registry keys they leave behind.
uninst.sort.name: Name
uninst.confirmText: The program's own uninstaller opens. Afterwards Tessera looks for leftovers.
uninst.maybe: The uninstaller finished, but {name} is still listed
uninst.leftNote: Folders go to the Recycle Bin; registry keys are backed up first and can be restored from the Registry page.
upd.title: Software updates
upd.sub: Updates installed programs through winget, the Windows Package Manager.
upd.noWinget: winget isn't installed. Get "App Installer" from the Microsoft Store.
upd.historySub: Updates done through Tessera. Roll one back if the new version gives you trouble.
upd.rbPin: Keep the old version (skip it in "Update all")
upd.rbText: Version {from} is installed over {to}. Your settings stay; the app may close while it installs.
upd.rbPinNote: It will be pinned, so updating everything skips it until you unpin it.
upd.confirmText: Programs are updated one at a time in the background. Some installers ask for administrator rights.
health.title: Disk health
health.sub: SMART status, temperature and wear of your drives, plus TRIM (SSD) or defragmentation (HDD).
health.needAdmin: Temperature, wear and error counters need administrator rights.
health.defragging: Defragmenting {v}; this can take a long time…
tray.boost_body: {game} is running with the boost settings
tray.update_body: The update left {size} behind. Open the Game library to clean it.
home.title: Home
home.sub: Your tiles at a glance. Pin more from any page with the pin next to its title, or here with Edit.
home.empty: No tiles pinned. Use Edit or the pin next to a page title.
pcs.title: Other PCs
pcs.sub: See the Care score, temperatures and free space of the other PCs at home. Only on your local network, read-only, and only between PCs you paired with a code.
pcs.shareSub: Let paired PCs see this one's status
pcs.firewall: Windows may ask once whether Tessera can use the network: allow it for private networks. A new code unpairs every PC that used the old one.
pcs.addSub: Turn on sharing there, then enter its address and the code it shows.
pcs.noneFound: No sharing PCs answered. Check that sharing is on and both are on the same network.
pcs.noneHint: Install Tessera on the other PC, turn on sharing there and pair it here.
tray.backup_body: {name}: {size} of new or changed files saved
rules.title: Your cleanup rules
rules.sub: Add your own folders to Smart cleanup: by folder name or full path, optionally only when they haven't changed for a while.
rules.none: No rules yet. For example: every "obj" folder, or C:\Projects\*\bin older than 30 days.
rules.name: Name
rules.kind.name: Folder name
rules.wildcards: * matches anything, ? one character. Upper and lower case don't matter.
rules.scanFirst: Scan a drive to see what the rule matches.
rules.typePattern: Type a pattern to see what it matches.
bench.title: Benchmark
bench.sub: A quick CPU, GPU, memory and disk test (about half a minute). Run it before and after a tweak or driver update to see what changed.
bench.runningHint: Keep other apps quiet while it runs for a fair result.
bench.noneHint: It never runs on its own: start it when you want a before / after comparison.
bench.historySub: Driver and profile changes between runs are marked, so a difference has a reason.
backup.title: Backup
backup.sub: Copies of chosen folders (documents, game saves) to another drive. Each backup is a complete dated folder, but unchanged files take no extra space.
backup.name: Name
backup.targetHint: Another drive keeps your files safe if this one fails. Backups go into a "Tessera Backup" folder there.
backup.noneHint: Pick your documents or game saves and a second drive. Tessera does the rest on a schedule.
backup.done: Backup done: {n} files copied, {linked} unchanged, {size} written
net.title: Network priority while gaming
net.sub: While a boosted game runs, these apps get a bandwidth cap so downloads don't push your ping up. The caps disappear when the game exits (and after a restart, whatever happens).
net.updates: Also slow down Windows Update downloads
net.updatesHint: Capped at 256 KB/s during the game, then put back exactly as it was.
upd2.title: Left behind by game updates
upd2.sub: Tessera noticed these games finished updating. Old downloads and outdated shader caches can go; shaders are rebuilt on the next launch.
upd2.confirmText: Everything goes to the Recycle Bin. The first launch may take a little longer while shaders are rebuilt.
gfx.title: Graphics presets
gfx.sub: Switch a game between competitive, balanced and quality settings, or fine-tune each level. Works with Unreal Engine games; the game's own settings file is changed and backed up first.
gfx.closeFirst: Close the game before saving: games write their settings file when they exit and would overwrite the change.
gfx.noneHint: Unreal Engine games create their settings file the first time you change something in their graphics menu.
sysjunk.old_downloads.hint: Files over 100 MB in Downloads, untouched for 6 months; they go to the Recycle Bin
gm.title: Game mode
gm.sub: When a game starts, Tessera can switch to full performance, close the apps you pick and put everything back when you quit. Every part is your choice.
gm.needAdmin: Clearing RAM, the full Gaming profile, core unparking and FPS recording need administrator rights.
gm.actionsSub: Turn on only what you want; everything is undone when the game exits
gm.act.switch_plan.hint: Ultimate or High performance while the game runs
gm.act.apply_profile.hint: Applies all Gaming tweaks, then your previous profile again
gm.act.clear_standby.hint: At start and whenever free memory runs low
gm.act.timer.hint: 0.5 ms system timer for smoother frame pacing
gm.act.unpark.hint: No waiting for parked cores to wake up
gm.act.reopen.hint: Starts them again when you quit the game
gm.act.record_fps.hint: Frame times are saved for the FPS page
gm.act.overlay.hint: Small always-on-top window during the game
gm.appsSub: Pick what gets closed and what must stay open. An app can only be on one list.
gm.perGameSub: Override the boost and app lists for single games, and set Windows options for their executables
gm.noExe: No game executable found in its folder
prompt.title: Boost {game}?
prompt.sub: Performance mode and your app list, undone when you quit
lib.title: Game library
lib.sub: Every installed game from Steam, Epic, GOG, Ubisoft, Xbox, EA, Battle.net, Riot and Rockstar in one place.
lib.sort.name: Name
lib.cleanupSub: Space games no longer need. Everything goes to the Recycle Bin.
lib.leftoversSub: Folders in your libraries no installed game owns
lib.shadersSub: Games not played for a month; rebuilt on the next launch
lib.cleanText: These folders go to the Recycle Bin.
fps.title: FPS & ping
fps.sub: Frame rate and frame times through PresentMon (nothing is injected into games), saved per session so you can compare before and after a change.
fps.needAdmin: Recording frame times needs administrator rights (Windows' event tracing).
fps.download: The first recording downloads PresentMon (1 MB) from its official GitHub release and checks its signature hash.
fps.idleHint: Boosted games are recorded automatically, or enter a game's exe above and press Record.
fps.ovIdle: Not recording. Press the FPS hotkey while in a game.
fps.ovAdmin: Run Tessera as administrator to count FPS.
fps.ovWaiting: Waiting for the game's first frames…
fps.ovNoGame: No game in front. Click into the game, then press the hotkey.
fps.ovNoFrames: The game sent no frames. Try borderless or windowed mode.
ov.title: FPS window
ov.sub: Shown over your game while it is recorded. Toggle it in a game with {key}. Exclusive fullscreen hides it; borderless works.
lat.title: Latency check
lat.none: Recorded before this check existed. Record the game again to see it.
lat.tipVsync: V-Sync is on and adds up to a frame of delay. Turn it off and cap the game at {cap} FPS (or use G-Sync / FreeSync).
lat.tipComposed: Frames go through the Windows desktop compositor, which adds a frame. Use fullscreen, or turn on "Optimizations for windowed games" on the Display page.
lat.tipGpu: The GPU is maxed out, so frames queue up. Turn on NVIDIA Reflex / AMD Anti-Lag in the game, or cap it around {cap} FPS.
lat.tipDropped: {pct}% of frames never reached the screen. A frame cap smooths this out.
lat.tipCap: You render far more frames than your {hz} Hz screen shows. That is fine for latency; cap it if you want less heat and noise.
lat.tipGood: Nothing to fix: frames go straight to the screen without extra delay.
stut.title: Stutter detective
stut.none: No noticeable hitches in this session.
stut.h.thermal: Most hitches came while the CPU or GPU slowed itself down from heat. Check the Temperatures page and clean the fans.
stut.h.disk: Most hitches came while the disk was busy: the game loading data, or an update or scan in the background. A faster SSD or fewer background apps help.
stut.h.background: Most hitches came while another app used a lot of CPU. Add it to game mode's close list.
stut.h.cpu: Most hitches came with the CPU fully loaded. Lower CPU-heavy settings (view distance, crowds, physics) or close background apps.
stut.h.gpu: Most hitches came with the GPU fully loaded. Lower resolution or heavy effects, or cap the frame rate.
stut.h.game: Nothing else was busy, so these are the game's own hitches, often shader compilation or streaming new areas. They usually fade after the first play.
slow.title: Why is my PC slow?
slow.sub: A one-click look at what is using the CPU, memory, disk and network right now, explained in plain words.
slow.snapshot: A one-second snapshot. Run it again while the PC feels slow.
slow.f.memory: Memory is {n}% full; {name} uses the most
slow.f.thermal: The {name} is slowing itself down because it is too hot
slow.f.fine: Nothing is holding your PC back right now
slow.h.cpu: Close it if you don't need it, or find it on the Background apps page.
slow.h.memory: When memory is full Windows swaps to the disk, which feels like stutter. Close big apps or browser tabs.
slow.h.disk: Everything that needs the disk waits. This often passes once an update, scan or download finishes.
slow.h.thermal: Hot chips run slower to protect themselves. Check the fans and airflow.
slow.h.startup: Many startup apps keep running in the background. Turn off the ones you don't need right away.
slow.h.fine: If it still feels slow, run the check again at that moment, or look at Temperatures and Disk health.
slow.known.launcher: A game launcher is downloading or updating
slow.known.malware_tool: The malware removal tool is running
slow.knownHint.defender: It runs after updates and on schedule. Leave it to finish; it usually takes a few minutes.
slow.knownHint.indexing: Search is reading new files. It settles down once it has caught up.
slow.knownHint.update: Updates are being installed in the background. Let them finish, then restart when it suits you.
slow.knownHint.telemetry: A short Windows check that runs now and then. It finishes on its own.
slow.knownHint.sync: Files are uploading or downloading. Pause sync in its tray icon if you need the speed now.
slow.knownHint.launcher: Pause the download in the launcher if you need the bandwidth or the disk.
slow.knownHint.compression: Memory is running short, so Windows packs it. Closing apps helps more than anything.
slow.knownHint.compositor: Usually high only with many windows, animations or several screens.
slow.knownHint.wmi: An app is asking Windows for system details. It is often a monitoring tool.
slow.knownHint.malware_tool: It runs after Windows updates and finishes on its own.
wake.title: Wake & sleep
wake.sub: What woke your PC up, what can wake it, and what keeps it from going to sleep.
wake.armed: Devices that can wake the PC
wake.armedSub: A bumped mouse or a network packet can wake it. Turn off the ones you don't need.
wake.noDevices: No device can wake the PC
wake.needAdmin: Changing what may wake the PC needs administrator rights.
wake.taskTitle: Scheduled tasks that wake the PC
wake.taskSub: These run on a timer even while the PC sleeps. Windows' own tasks are only listed.
wake.awakeSub: Apps and drivers that stop the screen or the PC from sleeping
wake.blockersAdmin: Windows only shows this to administrators.
wake.noBlockers: Nothing is keeping the PC awake
boot.timelineSub: Each start of Windows. Click one to see what slowed it down.
boot.cleanRun: Windows didn't flag anything slow on this boot.
boot.startupNow: Startup apps after the last boot
boot.startupNowSub: When each one started and how much memory it uses now
fps.noSessions: No recordings yet. Boosted games are recorded automatically.
ping.title: Ping
ping.hint: Pinging {host} once a second. High jitter or loss to your router points at Wi-Fi or cabling.
disp.title: Display & RAM
disp.sub: Refresh rate, Windows graphics options for games, CPU core parking, the system timer and cached memory.
disp.needAdmin: Core parking and clearing RAM need administrator rights.
disp.fixText: The screen may go black for a second while Windows changes the mode.
disp.lowHint: Your display can do {max} Hz but runs at {hz} Hz: games can't show more than {hz} FPS on it.
disp.graphicsSub: Windows' own switches; every change can be turned back
disp.sw.SwapEffectUpgradeEnable.hint: Lower latency and VRR for games in borderless windows
disp.sw.VRROptimizeEnable.hint: Lets G-Sync / FreeSync work in more games
disp.switchSaved: Setting saved; restart games to apply
disp.parkingHint: Keeps every core awake on AC power (now: at least {n}% unparked)
disp.timerHint: Current vs finest resolution; game mode asks for the finest while you play
ram.title: Memory
ram.sub: Windows keeps recently used files in standby memory. Clearing it can help with stutter on PCs with little RAM.
ram.hint: Safe: it's only a cache, Windows refills it as needed
temps.title: Temperatures
temps.sub: CPU and GPU temperatures, clocks, load and throttling, read without any extra drivers.
temps.noCpuTemp: This PC doesn't report a CPU temperature to Windows without a driver.
temps.noGpuTemp: This GPU doesn't report its temperature without the vendor's tools.
temps.throttleSub: Times the CPU or GPU slowed itself down because of heat or power limits
temps.trendSub: Rising idle temperatures over weeks usually mean dust in the fans
temps.trendWait: Tessera records idle temperatures once a day; the trend appears after a few days.
temps.dust: Idle temperature rose by {n} °C over the last weeks. Time to clean the fans and heatsinks.
bat.title: Battery
bat.sub: How much of its original capacity your laptop battery has left.
bat.noneSub: This PC runs on mains power only.
bat.historyWait: Tessera saves a reading once a day; the chart grows from here.
bat.worn: The battery lost {n}% of its capacity. Consider a replacement if runtime matters.
crash.title: Crashes & blue screens
crash.sub: App crashes, hangs, blue screens and power losses from the Windows event log, in plain words.
crash.none: No crashes in the last {n} days
crash.topSub: Update or reinstall what shows up most
crash.bsodHint: Blue screens are almost always drivers (graphics first), overclocks, RAM or heat. Update the driver named here and check the Temperatures page.
sec.title: Security checkup
sec.sub: The protections Windows has, and whether they are on. Tessera only reads; the buttons open the right Windows settings.
sec.defender.hint: Microsoft Defender (third-party antivirus shows as unknown)
sec.realtime.hint: Scans files as they are opened
sec.bitlocker.hint: BitLocker on the system drive protects data if the PC is stolen
sec.secure_boot.hint: Blocks boot-level malware; required by some anti-cheats
sec.uac.hint: Asks before apps make system changes
sec.bitlockerAdmin: Drive encryption status needs administrator rights.
boot.title: Boot time
boot.sub: How long Windows takes to start and which apps slow it down, from Windows' own boot measurements.
boot.needAdmin: Windows' boot performance log can only be read as administrator.
boot.slowSub: Apps and services Windows flagged as delaying startup
drv.title: Drivers
drv.sub: Graphics drivers matter most for games. Tessera shows how old yours is and opens the official download page.
drv.oldHint: This driver is {n} days old. New games often need newer drivers.
drv.storeSub: Windows keeps every previous driver after an update. Unused old versions can go; the newest and any in use always stay.
drv.storeAdmin: Listing the driver store needs administrator rights.
drv.storeClean: No old driver packages to remove
drv.storeConfirmText: None of them is used by a device, and a newer version of each stays installed. Windows refuses anything still in use.
wu.title: Windows Update
wu.sub: When Windows last updated, whether a restart is waiting, and a fix for updates that are stuck.
wu.needAdmin: Resetting the update cache needs administrator rights.
wu.rebootYes: A restart is needed to finish installing updates
wu.serviceHint: Runs on demand; idle is normal
wu.stale: The last update is {n} days old. Check Windows Update.
wu.pendingSub: Asks Microsoft's servers; can take a minute
wu.stuckHint: Stops the update services, sets the download cache aside and starts them again: the standard fix for failing updates.
wu.resetText: Windows downloads pending updates again afterwards. Nothing already installed is affected.
rep.title: Weekly report
rep.sub: What Tessera did for your PC: space freed, games played, health over time. Everything stays on this PC.
rep.nothingFreed: Nothing cleaned in this period yet.
rep.noGames: No game sessions recorded in this period.
rep.careWait: Run Care a few times to see the trend.
settings.widgetHint: A small window with CPU, GPU, RAM and FPS you can place anywhere
settings.weeklyHint: A notification once a week with what Tessera did
hotkeys.title: Global hotkeys
hotkeys.sub: Work everywhere, also inside games. Click a field and press the combination; Backspace clears it.
hotkeys.hint: Click, then press a key combination with Ctrl, Alt or Shift
hotkeys.taken: These hotkeys are used by another app: {keys}
io.title: Settings file
io.sub: Save your profiles, game mode lists, Care and app settings, and load them on another PC.
dism.title: Windows component cleanup
dism.sub: Removes old versions of Windows components left behind by updates (often 1–5 GB).
dism.confirmText: Windows removes superseded component versions with its own DISM tool. Afterwards, already installed updates can no longer be uninstalled.
